generator_and_origin.target: scripts/build_presentation.py:parse_enter_high_score_contract and the generated cursor/node destination contract
generator_and_origin.change: Shift each sprite-origin destination by +160 bytes, one bitmap scanline: cursor_destination and every node_destinations entry. Keep framebuffer_destination, PLAYER_CELL, action coordinates, name text destinations, wall art, and the 576-byte table length unchanged.
generator_and_origin.reason: The complete shared-text owner starts from cursor_destination. The legacy presentation name_draw_cursor path draws from node_destinations. Shifting only the initial cursor would create an owner-dependent one-scanline offset or a jump when legacy rendering snaps to a node.
generator_and_origin.callers: build_presentation.py and verify_presentation.py already receive explicit --chars, --gameplay-chars, --gameplay-sprites, and TMX inputs. Compile the 16 directional animation frames from the existing --gameplay-sprites input for the pixel hazard oracle; add no asset or CLI input.

edge_and_hazard_data.change: Retain low-nibble N/E/S/W edges and the 576-byte table. Apply the existing one-cell-left anchor overhang around authored code-49 inner-wall cells. Reuse the high nibble for four exact unordered perpendicular-pair flags at six-pixel offset: NE=$10, ES=$20, SW=$40, WN=$80.
edge_and_hazard_data.semantics: A set pair flag means some compiled animation-frame opaque pixel in any facing intersects an authored code-49 wall pixel along the complete current-position plus 2-pixel snap sweep. Swapping old and requested directions reverses the same position set, so four flags represent all eight directed tuples without directional false positives.
edge_and_hazard_data.boundary: Keep hazard flags zero on blocked/perimeter/top/right-anchor entries. Preserve low edge bits exactly after overhang processing and leave every aligned edge available unless the geometry mask itself blocks it.

runtime_rule.change: At a partial perpendicular turn, preserve the current low-edge test. For the six-pixel state ($DE==1), check the unordered direction-pair flag. A blocked requested edge or set hazard flag returns the existing handled/hold result; safe requests use the current snap path. A rejection leaves PLAYER_DIR, PLAYER_FB, PLAYER_CELL, and snap state unchanged. Preserve the existing attempted PLAYER_FACE update, neutral/resume, reversal, and accepted-turn behavior.
runtime_rule.callback_contract: name_can_move must keep its A zero/nonzero edge result and return the original full table byte in B to name_late_turn. The stage variant currently retains B. The ranking variant reuses B for its bit-selection loop; restoring the saved table byte after ANDA requires a projected +2 bytes in the copied name code, not an assembled result.

risks_and_exclusions.high_risk_basis: Hard-boundary headroom is only 3 copied-name bytes and 4 nonadaptive resident bytes; helper placement is reported at zero free bytes. Runtime owner, map, and origin integration need exact fit and live evidence.
rejected: Universal four-pixel turn window: rejects geometry-safe six-pixel turns and changes the main movement rule.
Requested-facing-only collision test: misses all-face six-pixel trajectories caused by attempted facing.
Prune every edge with a six-pixel collision: loses all 45 action cells in the retained geometry audit.
Separate dense or sparse hazard allocation: exceeds the fixed data budget or introduces another lookup; the exact four-pair flags fit statically in the existing high nibble.
risks_and_exclusions.excluded_scope: Ordinary gameplay behavior, new runtime owner/helper/module/protocol, loader/MMU changes, allocations or limits, wall art, name layout, action positions, input bindings, score/rank rules, and implementation before explicit renewed approval.
